docs.purpose: The main signed-in screen for browsing permit leads. Along the top it shows seven counters - total permits, active permits, new this week, upcoming pre-permits, and three Committee-of-Adjustment counts. Below that a filter panel narrows the feed by trade and other criteria, and the feed itself lists matching permits as cards the user can open. Intended for a signed-in user hunting for work, not for operators.
docs.data_story: It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through 3 contracts: `/api/admin/stats`, `/api/permits`, `/api/trades`. Behind those contracts, the data comes from `address_points`, `building_footprints`, `coa_applications`, `entities`, `information_schema.columns`, `lead_views`, `neighbourhoods`, `notifications`, `parcel_buildings`, `parcels`, `permit_parcels`, `permit_trades`, `permits`, `pg_class`, `pipeline_runs`, `pipeline_schedules`, `sync_runs`, `trade_mapping_rules`, `trades` and `wsib_registry`, and writes land on `pipeline_runs`.
docs.under_126: **REBUILD** — it drives writes, so a client decision has to be re-homed on the server before the projection can be honest. It renders through the DASHBOARD renderer (tiles that each declare their own contract and degrade independently), reading by reference: `/api/admin/stats`, `/api/permits`, `/api/trades`. Its `owns.components[]` declares `src/components/permits/PermitFeed.tsx`, `src/components/permits/PermitCard.tsx`, `src/components/search/FilterPanel.tsx` and `src/components/layout/MobileNav.tsx`.

emits: none — no captureEvent import in the page or in any of its four owned components

versioning.why: The stats payload is guarded field-by-field by isValidDashboardStats, which rejects any shape missing one of its six numeric fields — removing or retyping a field breaks the guard and blanks the row to `--`.

inputs.why: Three contracts, two of them reached by a component rather than by the page: /api/admin/stats from the page itself, /api/permits from PermitFeed and /api/trades from FilterPanel. All three are bare fetch calls — there is no hook to trace.

outputs.why: The page itself writes nothing. Note that its GET to /api/admin/stats reaches reapStaleRunningRows, which DOES update pipeline_runs server-side — a side effect of the contract, not of this surface.

state.why: Two useState hooks (filters, stats) plus PermitFeed's five — all component-local, none persisted, none read by another surface, so no Field Ownership Matrix field is owned here.

staleness.why: Every tile and the feed refetch from the route on mount with no cache between them — the page uses bare fetch, not TanStack Query, so the shell's 60s staleTime never applies to it.

session.why: classifyRoute('/dashboard') is 'authenticated' — it is not in PUBLIC_PATHS, and the middleware redirects a sessionless visitor to /login?redirect=/dashboard.

rls_class.why: Every table behind its three contracts is pipeline-owned and reached by the server-side pg pool through src/lib/db/client, not by a user-scoped Supabase client — default-deny with no policy, service-role only.

checks.why: The page is `authenticated` but one of its three contracts, /api/admin/stats, classifies as `admin` — the two do not agree, and today the mismatch is invisible only because that route carries no verifyAdminAuth of its own.

isValidDashboardStats must reject every non-stats shape (route 500, envelope 500, null, partial, null-field) — the unguarded setStats(data) white-screened the whole page on .toLocaleString() of undefined.

A failed stats fetch must leave the seven tiles reading `--` while FilterPanel and PermitFeed keep rendering from their own separate fetches; the .catch(() => {}) is what makes that true and it must stay.

errors.why: Neither failure path renders anything: the stats fetch ends in `.catch(() => {})` and a non-ok response sets null, so a 500 and a healthy-but-empty database are indistinguishable — both show `--`.

sharing.why: /api/permits is also rendered by the mobile feed and /api/trades by FilterPanel wherever it is mounted; /api/admin/stats is additionally rendered by the admin dashboard.
sharing.varies_by_surface: The admin dashboard reads the full stats payload; this page projects six of its fields into seven tiles, one of which (CoA Unlinked) is computed client-side as coa_total - coa_linked.

limitations.what: A non-admin signed-in user is served admin-scoped counts.
limitations.measured: /api/admin/stats classifies as `admin` (middleware.logic.test.ts:68) but carries no verifyAdminAuth (grep count 0 in src/app/api/admin/stats/route.ts), and the middleware admin arm is a session-presence check only (src/middleware.ts:115-121).

notes: No governing spec: absent from every system-map row and no SPEC LINK header. A signed-in NON-admin page that calls /api/admin/stats - classifyRoute puts /api/admin/* in the 'admin' class, so the stats fetch will 401 for a plain authenticated user; the page swallows it (.catch(() => {})) and the counters render as '--'. That swallow is also why there is no error state. PermitCard is reached only via PermitFeed. MobileNav is rendered only by this page. MEASURED 2026-09-15, two disagreements recorded. (1) AUTH-CLASS: the page is `authenticated` but /api/admin/stats is `admin`; it works today only because that route has no verifyAdminAuth (grep count 0) and the middleware admin arm checks session PRESENCE, so any signed-in non-admin gets the admin counts. (2) A GET WITH A WRITE: /api/admin/stats calls reapStaleRunningRows (route.ts:7), so this page's read updates pipeline_runs — recorded on outputs.why rather than in outputs.tables because the write belongs to the contract. Also measured: this page uses bare fetch + useState throughout, never TanStack Query, so the QueryClient the root shell mounts is inert for it. a11y.touch_target_min_px stays UNRESEARCHED — the pagination buttons are px-3 py-1.5 on text-sm = 32px, a value the vocabulary (UNRESEARCHED or integer >= 44) cannot express.

measured_gate.why: classifyRoute('/dashboard') matches no public or admin arm, is not in AUTHENTICATED_API_ROUTES, no PUBLIC_PREFIXES entry is a prefix of it, and it is not in PUBLIC_PATHS - it then hits the explicit `pathname.startsWith('/dashboard')` arm and returns 'authenticated'.
